rooms.12183: No lamp has ever been hung in this room, and the blackness is so thick that it seems to press against your eyes. Your hands find walls of rough, damp stone, and grit crunches underfoot at every step. Somewhere close a slow drip counts out the seconds. A thin line of light shows beneath a door to the north, where the Interrogation Centre lies, and the deserted corridor opens back to the west.
rooms.12177: Long trestle tables fill this low cellar, their tops chalked into numbered squares where whatever is taken from the prisoners is laid out, counted and tagged. A ledger is chained to the end of each table, its pages ruled into columns and filled in a small, patient hand. The smell of tallow and old leather hangs beneath the vaulted ceiling. Worn stone steps climb up to the Square, and a narrow doorway to the south opens on a sitting room.
rooms.12176: Someone has tried to make this cellar room comfortable, and the effort is more unsettling than bare stone would be. Two armchairs with faded rose covers face a cold hearth, and a tall clock stands against the wall, its pendulum stopped and its face painted with smiling suns. A threadbare rug hides most of the flagstones, though not the dark stain near its edge. The outlay lies through a doorway to the north, and a curtained alcove opens to the east.
rooms.12175: This narrow alcove is barely wider than a man's outstretched arms, closed off from the sitting room by a curtain of heavy brown velvet. A stone shelf runs along the back wall, crusted with the stubs of a hundred candles burned down to nothing. Above it, scratched into the plaster by many different hands, are rows of names, some of them crossed through. The curtain to the west is the only way out.
rooms.12112: The tunnel bores into the flank of Vice Hill through a frame of massive timbers, every one of them painted thick with black pitch. Daylight and the smell of grass reach a few paces in from the hillside to the west, then give up. Beyond them the walls glisten with tar that has run and hardened in long, rippled curtains. The passage leads north into the dark, and the air breathing out of it is warm and sharp with the reek of pitch.
rooms.12114: Tar seeps from cracks in the rock here and creeps down the walls in slow black beads, pooling wherever the floor dips. The pools have set hard enough to hold footprints, dozens of them, all pressed into the pitch and all heading north. Torch brackets of rusted iron are fixed to the walls at intervals, their sockets choked with soot. The tunnel runs on north and back south toward the hillside.
rooms.12116: A wide niche has been hacked out of the wall here to hold an iron cauldron, its belly cracked and its rim furred with layers of old pitch. The rock above it is scorched black, and the smell of burnt tar is so strong that your eyes water. Someone once kept a fire going here day and night to keep the walls freshly coated. Spilled tar has set in treacherous ridges across the floor, and the tunnel continues north and south.
rooms.12118: The rock gives way here to loose earth, and the roof is held up by tarred props and crossbeams that groan softly under their load. Black drips gather on the beams and fall now and then onto the floor, where they have built little cones of pitch like a field of tiny cairns. The air is close and warm, and every sound stops short against the walls. The tunnel leads north deeper into the hill and south toward the way out.
rooms.12120: Iron rings are set into both walls here at the height of a man's wrists, and the tar beneath each one is scuffed and gouged by the struggling of many feet. Long smears run along the floor where something, or someone, was dragged. The walls have been tarred so often that the hewn rock is lost beneath a smooth black skin that gleams in what little light there is. The passage goes on north and falls away south.
rooms.12122: The tunnel ends here against a wall of bare rock, scraped clean of tar in a broad square as if to make a page. Into it someone has chiselled words in tall, careful letters, now half filled with soot. A low doorway to the west opens on the Entrance To The Hall Of Hopelessness, and a chill draught flows out of it, carrying a smell of cold ashes. The only other way is back south along the tarry passage.
rooms.12184: A steep path scrambles up from Vice Hill into a wood of tall, wind-bent pines, their roots gripping the slope like knuckled fingers. The noise and smoke of the hill fade quickly, replaced by the creak of branches and the sigh of wind in the needles. Steps cut into the earth and edged with split logs lead down to the hillside below. Northward the path levels out and wanders on among the trunks.
rooms.12185: The pines grow close together here, and the light beneath them is a dim, rust-coloured gloom. A thick carpet of needles swallows the sound of your steps. Someone has blazed the trunks along the path with a hatchet, each cut daubed with red paint so that it can be followed by lantern light. The marks lead north into the wood and south toward the steps above Vice Hill.
rooms.12186: A great pine has come down across the path, and rather than clear it, someone has sawn a gap through the trunk just wide enough for a man with a load on his back. The earth in the gap is churned and grooved, as if heavy sledges are hauled through it often. Ferns crowd the hollow left by the torn-up roots, and the resin of the cut wood still scents the air. Beyond the fallen trunk the path goes on north, and it runs back south between the pines.
rooms.12187: A small stream crosses the path here in a stony bed, and two flat stones have been set in the water as a crossing. The pines thin a little around it, letting in a slanting light that turns the water amber. Moss grows thick on the boulders along the banks, and the air is cool and smells of wet earth. From somewhere ahead comes the faint, steady hush of surf. Over the stepping stones the path heads north, and it climbs back south into the trees.
rooms.12188: The wood changes here, the pines giving way to twisted holm oaks whose dark, leathery leaves rattle in the wind off the sea. Sand has begun to creep in among the leaf litter, pale and gritty underfoot. A tree beside the path has been hollowed by fire, and its blackened heart is just big enough to hide a man or a barrel. The path leads north toward the sound of the waves and south deeper into the pines.
rooms.12189: The trees here lean away from the wind, and between their trunks you catch glimpses of grey water and white breakers. The smell of salt and weed grows strong, and the ground is more sand than soil, held together by tufts of spiky grass. A rope strung from trunk to trunk along the path serves as a handrail, rubbed smooth by many palms. The path drops north toward Port By The Forest and rises back south into the wood.
rooms.12190: The trees come right down to the water in this sheltered cove, so close that their roots trail in the tide. A jetty of rough grey planks runs out from the shore on pilings green with weed, and a lantern post at its end is hooded so that its light would show only to the sea. A boathouse of logs stands under the pines with its doors chained shut. The only way out is the path that leads back south through the trees.
rooms.12109: Here at the foot of Vice Hill the slope meets a lane of beaten earth, and the dens of the hill begin. Gaudy lanterns of red and yellow paper hang from a line strung between two leaning posts, and a smell of spilled wine and cheap incense drifts on the air. A track of worn steps climbs up the slope toward the busier heights of the hill. The lane runs on south between thickets of gorse.
rooms.12110: The lane winds along the lower slope of Vice Hill between shacks of tarred driftwood, their doors painted with dice, cups and grinning faces to show what is sold within. Most stand shuttered, but the smell of smoke and stale beer clings to every plank. Broken crockery glints among the gorse at the roadside, where the hill's customers have flung their empties. North, the lane runs back toward the steps that climb the hill, and south it reaches a crossroads.
rooms.12128: Four ways meet at this crossroads on the shoulder of Vice Hill, marked by a tall post of black wood carved with a single staring eye. East of it a broad stair of stone climbs up onto the Trail of Terror, its steps spattered with drippings of red wax. The High Path runs off west along the ridge, the Cliff Road strikes south toward the sea cliffs, and the lane leads back north among the dens. The wind up here is cold and carries the smell of incense.
rooms.12130: The Trail of Terror begins at the head of a stair from Vice Hill and runs south along the hillside between high walls of soot-blackened stone. Iron cages hang from brackets above the street, creaking in the wind, empty but for a few rags snagged in their bars. Black candles burn in niches along the walls, and their wax has run down the stone in long tears. The stair leads back west to the crossroads.
rooms.12132: Masks are nailed to every door along this stretch of the trail, carved from pale wood and painted with faces caught in the moment of screaming. There are hundreds of them, so close together that the walls seem to howl without a sound. The cobbles underfoot are worn into a shallow trough down the middle, as if by countless processions. Southward the trail goes on toward the temple, and northward it returns to the head of the stair.
rooms.12134: A gibbet of black oak stands over the trail here, its arm reaching out across the street and its chain ending in an empty iron collar. Beneath it a stone slab is carved with a long list of names, each followed by a single word for what that person feared most. The smell of incense grows heavier, drifting along the street from the south. Shuttered houses line the trail as it runs on south and back north.
rooms.12136: The walls on either side of the trail are painted with eyes, thousands of them, white and staring, from the gutters to the eaves. Whoever painted them took care that wherever you stand, some of them look straight at you. A dead tree grows through a crack in the paving, its bare branches hung with little bundles of hair and bone tied up in red thread. Under the low grey sky the trail continues north and slopes south toward the temple doors.
rooms.12138: The trail ends before the great door of the Temple of Terror, which fills the south side of the street behind a portico of squat black columns. The door is sheathed in iron and studded with nails whose heads are shaped like screaming faces, and a heavy knocker in the shape of a fist hangs at its centre. Smoke of incense seeps out around its edges, sweet and choking. Back to the north the trail runs between its painted walls.
rooms.12197: Beyond the iron door the temple swallows the daylight in a narthex of black marble, its walls polished so smooth that your own shape moves dimly in them. Censers hang on chains from the ceiling and breathe out a heavy, honeyed smoke that stings the throat. To the east a hard white light pours from the mouth of a hallway, too bright to look into. A passage leads south toward the high priest's office, and the door to the trail stands north.
rooms.12198: Light floods this hallway from every side, from hundreds of oil lamps set before polished brass mirrors that line the walls from floor to ceiling. The glare is so fierce that you must squint through your fingers, and the mirrors swim in a white haze. The heat of the flames is stifling. Through the glare you can make out an arch to the north leading to a shrine, while the hall runs on east and back west to the temple entrance.
rooms.12199: After the glare of the hallway, this small shrine is lit only by a ruby lamp, and its red dusk is a relief to the eyes. On a dais of veined marble sits a fat, smiling idol of gilded wood with six arms, each of them holding out some token of appetite. The floor before it is worn into two smooth hollows by the knees of worshippers. The only way out is south into the light.
rooms.12200: Here the light pours from a great chandelier of crystal prisms, ablaze with candles and scattering hard white sparks across every surface. The floor is tiled in white enamel that throws the glare back into your face until walls and floor blur into one blaze. Ropes of black velvet hang along the walls for the blinded to follow. Double doors to the north open into the Grand Temple Of Terror, and the hallway continues east and west.
rooms.12204: The nave of the Grand Temple rises into a darkness that the light of its braziers cannot reach, and the sense of something vast watching from that darkness is hard to shake. Rows of black pews face an altar of rough basalt, and behind it hangs an enormous mask of beaten silver, its mouth stretched wide in a frozen shriek. The air is thick with incense and the smell of hot iron. A door to the east leads back to the temple entrance, and the bright hallway lies south.
rooms.12202: The hallway ends in a blank wall of polished silver, curved like the inside of a bowl, that gathers the light of a ring of lamps and hurls it back down the passage in a single blinding beam. Standing here is like standing inside the sun; your shadow vanishes and your eyes run with tears. The stone underfoot is warm to the touch. The blazing hall leads back west, the only way out.
rooms.12192: This antechamber is panelled in dark wood carved with writhing figures, and a long bench runs along one wall for those summoned to wait upon the high priest. A brass plate on the south door bears his title, polished bright by his attendants. The air smells of ink, sealing wax and the incense that drifts in from the temple through the door to the north. A black curtain to the west hides the way into the Hall Of Death.
rooms.12195: The high priest's office is a room of unsettling neatness: a broad desk of black wood bare but for an inkstand, shelves of ledgers bound in grey leather, and a tall chair whose carved back curves over like a hood. Behind the desk hangs a map of Port Halyon, its streets studded with little red pins, one for each house the temple watches. A smell of warm tallow comes through an archway to the west, where the Hall Of Wax lies. The antechamber is back to the north.
rooms.12191: Figures of wax stand in rows along this long hall, each on its own plinth, each a man or woman caught in a moment of terror so lifelike that you half expect to hear them scream. Their glass eyes follow the flicker of the candles set at their feet. The air is warm and thick with the smell of tallow and something sweeter beneath it. A door to the north leads to the Hall Of Death, and the high priest's office lies through an arch to the east.
rooms.12194: Stone biers stand in two rows down this cold hall, each covered by a grey sheet that sinks into the hollows of the shape beneath. A deep channel cut in the floor runs between them to a grated drain, stained dark along its length. Bunches of dried herbs hang from the beams, failing to mask the smell. The Hall Of Torture opens to the north, a door leads south to the Hall Of Wax, and an archway east returns to the high priest's antechamber.
rooms.12193: Here the temple keeps its instruments on display as proudly as a guildhall keeps its silver: the rack, the wheel, the scold's bridle and a dozen stranger devices, each on its own stand with a brass plaque beneath. Everything is oiled, polished and in good repair. Chains hang from rings in the vaulted ceiling, and the floor slopes gently toward a drain at the centre. A doorway to the east leads to the high priest's antechamber, and the Hall Of Death lies south.
rooms.12140: The Cliff Road leaves the crossroads on Vice Hill and strikes out along the brink of the sea cliffs, a ledge of bare grey rock hardly wide enough for a cart. On one side the cliff rises in cracked and weathered terraces; on the other it drops sheer to the surf boiling far below. The wind tears at your cloak and fills your mouth with salt. The road runs on south and back north to the hill.
rooms.12141: A chain as thick as your thumb has been pinned to the rock face along this stretch, giving travellers something to cling to where the ledge narrows to a few feet. Its links are rusted orange except where hands have gripped them bright. Far beneath, the sea surges into a cleft in the cliff and booms like a drum. With the chain to guide you, the road edges on north and south.
rooms.12142: Here the road passes a shallow overhang in the cliff face, where travellers have sheltered from the wind and left the black smudges of old fires on the rock. Clumps of sea thrift cling to the ledges, nodding pink heads in the gusts. Out over the water the horizon is lost in grey haze. The ledge leads north toward Vice Hill and south to where the road comes to an end.
rooms.12143: The Cliff Road comes to an abrupt end here, where a great slice of the cliff has fallen into the sea and taken the road with it. The broken edge is raw and pale, and a heap of stones has been piled at the brink as a warning, topped with the bleached skull of a goat. Beyond the gap the old roadway can be seen running on along the cliffs, out of reach. There is nowhere to go but back north.
rooms.12129: The High Path leaves the crossroads on Vice Hill and runs along the spine of the ridge, a narrow street paved with slabs of grey slate. Tall, thin houses lean together on either side, their upper floors jutting out so far that the strip of sky above is no wider than a hand. Iron lamp brackets shaped like grasping claws hang above the doors. The path turns south along the ridge, and the crossroads lies back to the east.
rooms.12131: A gap between the houses here opens onto a sweeping view: the roofs of Port Halyon spread out far below, and beyond them the grey expanse of the Sea of Storms stretches to the horizon. A low parapet guards the drop, its stones carved with the initials of lovers and the names of the drowned. The slates of the street are slick with sea mist. The path follows the ridge north and south.
rooms.12133: The High Path narrows here to a stepped alley between blank walls that shut out all but a thread of grey daylight. Doors are few and all of them bolted, and the windows high above are fitted with iron grilles. Pale crusts of wax are stuck to every tread, dripped from the candles of some procession that passed this way. The alley runs on north and south.
rooms.12135: A little square opens on the High Path here around a well with a domed stone cover, its iron lid locked fast with a chain. Lantern posts stand at each corner of the square, their glass panes painted black so that they give only a thin red glimmer. On the wall of one house a faded mural shows a procession of hooded figures winding toward a temple on a hill. From the square the path leads on north and south.
rooms.12137: The High Path ends at a low side door set deep in the wall of the Temple of Terror, whose dark bulk rises above the last of the houses. The door is narrow and plain, but a smell of warm tallow seeps from around its frame, and the step before it is crusted with drips of wax. This is the way the temple's servants come and go unseen. The door leads south into the Hall Of Wax, and the path runs back north along the ridge.
rooms.12104: This sunken courtyard lies below the Beachside Harem, hidden from the world by high walls of pink plaster faded almost white by the sun. A long pool of blue tiles fills its centre, though its water is green and still, and silk awnings that once shaded the cushioned benches hang in rags from their poles. Jasmine has run wild over the walls, and its sweet scent is heavy in the warm air. A flight of steps leads up to the Beachside Harem.
rooms.8869: The cliffs of the Island of Morvoct rise close at hand here, black and streaked with salt, and the swell surges against their foot in great bursts of spray. A cave mouth gapes in the cliff to the south, broad enough to take a boat, and the sea runs into it with a hollow roar. Your boat lurches and spins in the backwash. Open water lies north and west, back toward the Basalt Pillars.
rooms.15188: Here the Southern Sea Of Storms pours into a long tunnel of black rock that runs right through the cliffs of Morvoct, and a ledge cut along one wall gives a footing above the surging water. The roof arches high overhead, hung with dripping weed, and every wave that rolls in from the north fills the tunnel with booming echoes. Green daylight glimmers at the far end to the south, where the dock lies. The rock is slick and cold, and the air tastes of salt.
rooms.15100: A dock of massive stone blocks lies at the mouth of the sea tunnel, where the water calms into a clear pool walled by cliffs and open to a sky of racing cloud. Grass grows thick between the blocks, and the iron mooring rings are rusted almost through, for few boats tie up here. Beyond the dock a slope of turf and sea thrift rises toward a wall of dark stone and its gate. The tunnel leads back north to the open sea, and a paved way climbs south to the gate.
rooms.15101: A wall of green-black stone runs across the island here, and in it stands the Gate To Kyor'Glt, two leaves of bronze gone blue with age and carved with faces that have the round, lidless eyes of fish. The gates are shut and barred from the far side, and thorny sea-buckthorn has grown up thick against them. Through a crack between the leaves an untravelled path can just be seen, lost under weeds. The only open way leads north, back to the dock.
rooms.8862: The Basalt Pillars stand just to the north, a cluster of black columns so tall that the low clouds seem to snag on them, and the swell piles up white against their bases. The water here is deep and dark, cold enough that the spray stings like sleet. Away to the east the cliffs of an island loom out of the haze. Southward and westward the open sea heaves in long grey ridges.
rooms.8861: Your boat drifts among the Basalt Pillars Of Stethelos, a forest of six-sided columns of black stone that rise sheer from the sea, some taller than any tower in Port Halyon, others broken off into stumps barely awash. The currents swirl between them in contrary directions, so that the water seems to boil without heat. Sounds echo strangely here, coming back from the stone a heartbeat late. Channels open between the pillars to the north, east, south and west.
rooms.8879: North of the Basalt Pillars the current takes hold of your boat and pulls it sideways in a long, curving glide, as if the sea itself were circling something. The columns crowd close behind to the south, their black flanks glistening with spray. Patches of foam spin slowly on the surface, gathered into rings. Clear water lies north, while to the east the current runs on in its strange sweep.
rooms.8859: A great black stack of rock rises from the sea close beside your boat, its sides sheer and streaked with white, its top crowned with a ragged tuft of grass. The swell breaks against it with a deep, shuddering thud you can feel through the hull. There is no landing anywhere on its walls. Open water runs north and east, and the tall shapes of the Basalt Pillars stand not far off to the south.
rooms.8858: Out here the swell runs long and heavy, and your boat climbs each grey ridge slowly before sliding down its back into the trough. Tangled mats of yellow weed drift on the surface, lifting and falling with the water. Far off, the dark columns of the Basalt Pillars break the horizon like the teeth of a broken comb. Not a sail shows anywhere on the sea that stretches north, east, south and west.
rooms.8850: The black stack of rock looms close by here, so near that its shadow falls across your boat and turns the water beneath it the colour of ink. Its base is fringed with jagged ledges over which the swell pours in sheets of white, and the roar of it fills the air. No boat could pass the rock, but open water leads north, east and west.
rooms.8841: Here the sea is a dull pewter grey under a low, unbroken sky, and a cold drizzle hangs in the air without ever quite falling. The swell is short and choppy, and your boat bucks and slaps from one wave to the next. Ahead, the sheer black shape of a sea stack shows through the murk. Grey water spreads north, east, south and west.
rooms.8842: Waves smash against the flank of the great black stack just beyond your bow, and the backwash shoves your boat away from the rock in a smother of foam. At the waterline the stone is crusted thick with mussels and barnacles, and long ropes of weed stream from it in the surge. Close as it is, the rock offers no landing and no way past. Open water lies north, south and west.
rooms.8843: Beneath your boat, through water as clear as green glass, a line of great squared stones runs along the sea floor, straight as a road and far too regular to be the work of the sea. Weed waves from the joints between them, and here and there a fallen column lies across the line. The drowned road seems to lead on toward the distant Basalt Pillars. The sea is open all around, north, east, south and west.
rooms.8852: The great stack of black rock towers close above your boat here, its face scored by deep cracks where the sea has been working at it for ages. A shelf of tumbled boulders lies at its foot, and the swell sucks and gurgles among them like something breathing. The black columns of the Basalt Pillars crowd the view not far beyond. Away from the rock, the water runs east, south and west.
rooms.8860: The Basalt Pillars rise just south of here, and already the current among them reaches out to tug at your boat, turning its bow this way and that. The water is laced with long streaks of foam that all point the same way, like the lines on a sailor's chart. Somewhere among the columns a hollow booming sounds at every swell. Easier water lies north, east and west.
rooms.8853: A drowned road surfaces here, or nearly: the tops of its great squared stones show just beneath the water, and waves break over them in a long white line that leads east to the foot of the Basalt Pillars. Beside it stand the stumps of two fluted columns, green with weed, that may once have flanked a gate. A careless oarsman could rip the bottom out of his boat on the stones. Deeper water lies north, south and west.
rooms.8854: A thick sea fog has settled over the water here, so dense that the bow of your boat fades into it. Sounds carry strangely: the slap of waves, the creak of the oars, and now and then a deep boom from somewhere close by, where the sea strikes stone. The fog smells of brine and of something older, like a cellar long shut. Blindly you may steer north, east, south or west.
rooms.8855: A squall of hail sweeps across the water, rattling off the boards of your boat and beating the sea into a dimpled grey. The wind gusts from all sides at once, and the waves stand up short and steep, slopping over the bow. Through a rent in the cloud you glimpse the dark cliffs of an island not far off. When the squall passes, the way will lie open north, east, south and west.
rooms.8863: The water runs fast and smooth here over a reef just beneath the surface, and your boat slides along it as if on a sheet of green glass. Where the reef ends, the sea breaks in a line of white water that no boat could cross. Beyond the breakers the black cliffs of the Island of Morvoct rise sheer out of the sea. The only safe water lies north and west.
rooms.8856: The swell rolls in from the open sea and breaks over a line of submerged rocks here, throwing up fountains of spray that drift across your boat like rain. A broken spar wedged between two of the rocks is all that remains of some vessel that found them first. Past the reef the sea is a churning white maze that no boat could survive. Calmer water lies north and west.
rooms.8847: A cold current wells up from the depths here, and the water turns suddenly dark and clear, so clear that you can gaze down into a blue gloom without a bottom. The chill rising from it makes your breath smoke even by day. Far below, faint shapes like the tops of towers seem to show and fade again as the light shifts. Above that abyss your boat may go north, east, south or west.
rooms.8846: The sea runs in long, tall rollers here, so steep that your boat stands almost on its stern as it climbs each one and then plunges into the trough beyond. At the top of each wave you glimpse a far line of pale dunes; at the bottom, nothing but grey walls of water. The wind hums in the oarlocks. The rollers march on unbroken north, east, south and west.
rooms.8845: Thunder rolls over this stretch of sea from a storm that stalks the horizon on long legs of rain. Every few heartbeats lightning shivers down into the water far off, and the whole sea flashes white and then goes dark again. The air tingles and smells sharp, like struck flint. The waves are building, and the storm-lit water stretches north, east, south and west.
rooms.8844: Kelp grows up from the sea floor here in a vast swaying forest, and its long brown fronds reach the surface and spread out in a slick, rubbery mat. Your oars tangle in it at every stroke, and the boat slows almost to a stop. Beneath the canopy of weed the water is shadowed and still. Clear channels lead out of the kelp to the north, east, south and west.
rooms.8835: The sea is calm here beneath a high, hazy sky, and the sun lays a path of dazzling white across the water that hurts to look at. Your boat rocks gently on a low swell. A raft of driftwood and tangled rope has been caught in some trick of the currents and turns slowly in place, going nowhere. The glittering water lies open north, east, south and west.
rooms.8834: Through the clear green water a sunken road can be seen, its great slabs cracked and tilted as if by some ancient upheaval. A carved stone head as big as your boat lies on its side among them, gazing up at you with blank, weed-fringed eyes. Long weed streams from its open mouth like a beard. Your boat can pass over the ruins to the north, east, south or west.
rooms.8833: A strong current sets across this stretch of sea, and you must row hard just to hold your place, the water streaming past the hull in long, twisting ropes. It flows toward a black stack of rock that juts from the sea not far off like a broken tooth. The waves are short and confused where the current meets the swell. Fighting the current, you may still make way north, east, south or west.
rooms.8832: The bottom falls away here into deep water, and the sea changes from green to a dark, inky blue. The swell grows longer and heavier, and your boat begins to rise and fall in a slow rhythm that makes the stomach lurch. Behind you the coast has dwindled to a low grey line. Deep water spreads north, east, south and west.
rooms.8824: A beacon stands here on a reef that barely breaks the surface, a tall post of tarred timber topped with an iron basket for a fire. The basket is cold and rusted, and the post leans at an angle, battered by years of waves. Around its foot the water foams over the hidden rocks. Giving the reef a wide berth, you may steer north, east, south or west.
rooms.8825: Nothing but water lies on every hand here, grey and restless under a sky of low, racing cloud. The coast has sunk out of sight, and the only way to judge your course is by the run of the swell and the set of the wind. A lonely wind whistles over the wave tops. The sea stretches north, east, south and west, and all four ways look alike.
rooms.8826: The water is shallow here over a broad bank of white sand, and the sea turns a pale, milky green above it, glowing as if lit from beneath. Ripples in the sand below mirror the ripples on the surface. A line of great squared stones runs across the bank and out into the deeper water, too regular to be anything but the work of hands. From the bank the sea opens north, east, south and west.
rooms.8827: A slow whirlpool turns here, wide as a village green, its rim marked by a ring of spinning foam and drifting weed. Your boat is drawn sideways along the edge of it before you can pull clear, and the hull groans as the water twists beneath. At its heart the sea sinks into a shallow, glassy dimple. Pulling free of the rim, you can head north, east, south or west.
rooms.8828: The end of a long spit of black boulders lies close beside your boat here, reaching out from the shore and ending in a jumble of rocks that the waves pour over. A crooked iron pole has been driven into the last boulder as a warning, its tip hung with a tangle of old rope. There is no way across the spit. Open water lies north, east and south.
rooms.8836: The wind blows steadily here from the land, carrying a fine dust that settles on the water and on your boat, gritty and warm. It smells of hot stone and dry grass, the breath of the desert beyond the coast. The waves are low and orderly, marching away from the shore in neat ranks. Dusty water lies open north, east, south and west.
rooms.8837: A sheen of dark oil spreads across the water here, painting the swells with slow rainbows, and a smell of rancid fish hangs over it. It wells up from somewhere far below, perhaps from the cargo of a whaler lying on the sea floor. Your oars come up black and greasy. Beyond the slick the sea runs clean to the north, east, south and west.
rooms.8838: Long lines of foam stretch across the water here, marking a meeting of currents where the sea is wrinkled and choppy. Your boat jolts as it crosses each line, and the bow swings of its own accord. Away beyond the low waves, a coast of pale sand shimmers in the heat haze. Across the choppy lines you may steer north, east, south or west.
rooms.8839: Dunes of pale gold come down almost to the water's edge here, and the breakers roll up a broad beach of sand so bright in the sun that it hurts the eyes. Hot wind blows off the land, and grains of sand patter on the boards of your boat. The surf is far too heavy to beach a boat safely. Open water lies north and east.
rooms.8848: The surf booms against a low cliff of crumbling yellow sandstone here, carved by the waves into arches, pillars and caves. Sand streams from the clifftop in thin, glittering falls whenever the wind gusts. The sea heaves and sucks among the rocks at the cliff foot. Your boat can stand off from the cliff to the north or the west.
rooms.8830: The water is shallow and warm here, close under the shore, and the swell rolls in long and lazy over a bottom of rippled sand. Beyond the breakers the coast is low and bare, a waste of dunes with a few tufts of grey grass. The bleached ribs of an old fishing boat stick up from the beach like the bones of some great fish. The sea runs north and east from these shallows.
rooms.8829: Gusts come off the land here in hot, sudden bursts, flattening the wave tops and spinning little whirls of spray across the water. Between the gusts the sea is strangely still. The spit of black rocks shows close by, waves breaking white along its length. Water lies open north, east, south and west, though the gusts make steering hard.
rooms.8822: Your boat rides in a pocket of quiet water here, hemmed in by the long spit of black rocks on one side and the shore on the other. The swell can barely reach this corner, and the water lies still and brown with sand stirred from the bottom. Weed rots in heaps along the rocks, and the smell is thick and green. The only way out is east, back to open water.
rooms.8820: A ridge of black boulders runs out from the shore here and blocks the way like a wall, the swell heaving and bursting against it in white fans of spray. Between the boulders, pools of trapped water flash in the light. The rocks are slick with weed and cannot be crossed. Open water lies north, east and west of the ridge.
rooms.8819: A light rain falls on this stretch of sea, pocking the surface with countless tiny craters and hushing the slap of the waves to a whisper. The coast is a smudge of grey through the rain, without detail or colour. Water drips from the brim of your hood and collects in the bottom of the boat. Through the rain the sea lies open north, east, south and west.
rooms.8818: A wreck lies on a hidden shoal here, a merchant ship heeled over on her side with half her hull out of the water and her masts long gone. Waves wash through the holes in her planking, and her name has been scoured off her stern by the sea. The shoal around her is marked by a ring of choppy, broken water. Clear of the shoal, the sea runs north, east, south and west.
rooms.8817: The wind has torn the clouds into long white streamers here, and the sun comes and goes, chasing patches of light and shadow across the water. The sea shifts colour with them, from green to grey to a bright, hard blue. Behind you the towers of Port Halyon stand along the shore under a haze of chimney smoke. The changing water runs on north, east, south and west.
rooms.8811: An old ship's hull lies at anchor here, dismasted and stripped, kept afloat as a store hulk for the port. Her sides are black with tar and patched with mismatched planks, and every gunport has been boarded shut. The great anchor chain that holds her slants into the green water, furred with weed. Around the hulk the sea lies open north, east, south and west.
rooms.8812: A sandbank lies just beneath the surface here, a long pale tongue under the green water, and the waves rear up and break as they pass over it. At low tide its crest must show, for a stake has been driven into it with a tattered red rag tied to the top. The water on either side of it is deeper and calmer. You can steer around the bank to the north, east, south or west.
rooms.8813: A row of tall stakes marches across the water here, the remains of a fish weir built long ago by the people of the shore. Most of the wattle between them has rotted away, leaving only the weathered posts, each capped with a tuft of weed left by the last high tide. The current hisses as it pours between them. Gaps in the old weir let your boat through north, east, south or west.
rooms.8814: The coast draws close here, a line of red-brown cliffs with a narrow cove biting into them to the south. The water near the cliffs is flecked with foam and strewn with floating weed. Your boat rises and falls on a swell that is beginning to feel the bottom. Open water lies north and east, and the shore curves away to the west.
rooms.8815: Your boat has come into a narrow cove between red cliffs, where the swell runs in long and smooth and breaks on a tiny beach of grey pebbles. The cliffs rise so high and close that the light in here is dim and green, and the sound of the waves echoes back and forth between them. Ferns hang from the wet rock. The cove opens only to the north, back to the sea.
rooms.8809: The shore is close at hand here, a beach of grey shingle where the waves break with a long, rattling roar as they drag the stones back with them. Above the beach rise low cliffs of red earth, crumbling and furred with grass. The surf is too strong to land in. Only to the north and east does the water open out.
rooms.8808: Brown river water fans out into the sea here, staining the green swell with clouds of silt and carrying twigs, leaves and tufts of reed out from the land. The meeting of fresh and salt water makes a ragged line of froth across the surface. Behind you the harbour light stands on its mole at the mouth of Port Halyon. Water lies open north, east and south, and the shore is close to the west.
rooms.8807: This is the outer anchorage of Port Halyon, where ships wait for the tide or a berth, and great mooring buoys of iron-banded timber bob on the swell at intervals. The water is churned and dirty, streaked with the slops of galleys. To the west the harbour light marks the entrance to the port. Open sea lies north, east and south.
rooms.8806: Just off the coast the swell begins to gather strength, and your boat lifts and falls on long grey waves that roll in from the open sea. Looking back, you can see the canal mouth and the tall crane of the unloading dock standing against the roofs of the port. The salt wind is strong and steady. Open water lies north, east and south, and the shoreline lies west.
rooms.8802: Your boat rocks in the choppy water off the mouth of the canal, where brown town water spills into the sea and the smell of tar, fish and rotting rope hangs over the waves. The unloading dock stands just to the west, its great crane leaning out over the canal mouth. The shoreline runs on north toward the ocean dock and south toward the harbour mouth. Open sea lies east.
rooms.8803: Two long moles of piled stone reach out from the shore here to embrace the harbour of Port Halyon, and between their heads lies the narrow entrance to the west. On the end of the nearer mole stands the harbour light, a squat round tower with a lantern room of iron and glass. The water at the harbour mouth is choppy where the tide runs out against the swell. The shoreline runs north and south, and the open sea lies east.
rooms.8804: Sandbars lie just beneath the surface along this stretch of shore, and the waves break over them in long lines of white. On the land, a fringe of salt marsh and reed beds marks where the river meets the sea, and to the west the river's mouth opens between low, muddy banks. The harbour moles stand to the north. Your boat can put out to open water east.
rooms.5086: The river slows and spreads as it nears the sea, its brown water swirling lazily between banks of reed and grey mud. Here the incoming tide pushes back against the current, and your boat turns slowly in confused little waves. North, the river opens into the harbour of Port Halyon, and east it runs out along the shoreline to the sea. Upstream to the west the river widens between its banks.
rooms.8800: Your boat floats in the broad harbour of Port Halyon, sheltered behind its stone moles from the worst of the sea. Quays of dressed stone line the shore, crowded with warehouses, and the masts of moored ships bristle against the sky. North lies the mouth of the canal and the great crane of the unloading dock, east the narrow harbour entrance, and south the mouth of the river. The water is green and smells of tar and fish.
rooms.12012: A towpath of beaten earth runs beside the canal here, its grassy verge trodden bare by the horses that haul barges toward the docks. The green canal water lies still and deep between its stone walls, flecked with chaff. Eastward the path leads to the warehouse dock, and westward it runs toward an old gate at the edge of the town. Elder bushes grow along the bank, grey with dust.
rooms.8880: The current that sweeps around the Basalt Pillars runs strongest here, and your boat is carried along on it like a leaf in a millrace. The pillars wheel slowly past, black against the sky, and it is hard to be sure which side of them you are on. Eddies twist the water into whirling knots. The current pulls south, while calmer water lies north and the way back runs west.
rooms.8881: Here the current doubles back on itself, and the water heaps up in a standing wave that never breaks and never moves, a ridge of green glass humming with power. Your boat slides along its foot. The Basalt Pillars rise close to the west, and between them the sea seethes white. The current runs on north and south.
rooms.8882: The current slackens here in a pool of black, glassy water ringed by reefs that show as dark shadows beneath the surface. Nothing breaks the stillness but the drip from your oars. The Basalt Pillars stand somewhere behind you, though when you look for them they seem to have moved. Channels between the reefs lead north and west.
rooms.8883: The currents here pull four ways at once, and your boat turns in slow circles no matter how you steer. The Basalt Pillars loom to the north, closer than they should be, though you were sure they lay behind you. A narrow race of fast water leads east between two reefs, and the open sea lies south and west. Mist drifts across the water in thin, curling veils.
rooms.8884: Your boat shoots through a narrow race between two long reefs, the water roaring white on either side and the hull shuddering as it skims the shallows. Spray hangs in the air like smoke. There is no turning back against a current this strong. The race bends and carries you on toward the north, where the water flattens and turns a strange, deep green.
rooms.8885: The water here is a deep, unnatural green, and light seems to rise from somewhere far below it, glowing faintly through the swell. To the west a great arch of green stone stands out of the sea, and the waves seem to bow as they pass beneath it. The open sea lies north, and the roaring race leads back south. The air is utterly still, and the sound of the surf seems very far away.
rooms.8886: A colossal arch of green stone rises out of the sea here, its pillars carved with spiralling figures worn smooth by ages of waves. Beneath it the sea does a thing that the sea should not do: it parts in a ring around a dark stairwell, held back as if by glass, and green stairs wind down into the depths. The water around the gate is calm and silent. Open sea lies north, east and west, and the stairs lead down.
rooms.8887: The stairs wind down through a shaft of green stone, polished and translucent, through which the sea can be seen pressing on every side, dim and silent. The steps are narrow and worn into hollows by feet long gone, and there is no rail. Above, a circle of grey light marks the gate; below, the stairs turn out of sight into darkness. A heavy door of green bronze is set in the wall to the west.
rooms.8890: This round chamber has four doorways, one in each wall, and every one of them opens back onto the green stairs, though never quite where you entered. Skeletons sit slumped against the walls between the doorways, dozens of them, as if they wandered from door to door until they could walk no more. The air is dead and dry, and the dust on the floor is printed with circling footsteps. North, south, east or west, the stairs wait.
rooms.8888: Midway down, the green stairs pass through a landing where the walls grow thick and opaque, and the light of the sea fades to a faint emerald glow from the stone itself. Archways open north and south off the landing, both leading into the same round chamber beyond. The steps continue up toward the gate and down into a deepening silence. Faint words are cut into each step, most of them worn almost away.
rooms.8889: The green stairs end here at a small landing deep below the sea, where the air is cold and still and smells of dust rather than salt. A tall door of black bronze stands in the east wall, cold to the touch, and a draught moves beneath it with a faint sigh. An open archway to the north and a smaller door to the west both lead into a low vault. The stairs climb up into the green glow.
rooms.8891: A long, low vault stretches away from the stairs, lined on both sides with stone coffins whose heavy lids have been pushed aside, all from within. Grave dust lies thick on everything, and the coffins hold nothing now but scraps of yellowed linen. Carved on the end wall is a great relief of a robed figure whose face is hidden behind a pale mask. A door leads east back to the stairs, and an archway to the south opens onto them as well.
rooms.8892: The bronze door opens in the foot of a great wall, and beyond it lies a city that cannot be here: Lost Carcosa, its towers rising into a dim sky where black stars hang even by day. The air is still and cool and utterly silent, without wind, bird or voice. Two pale suns sit low behind a haze, and every shadow is long. A broad street leads east into the city, and the door in the wall leads back west to the stairs.
rooms.8893: Tall houses of grey stone line this street, their windows empty and dark, their doors standing open on rooms where nothing stirs. Grey dust lies over the paving in a smooth, unbroken layer, so fine that it rises in slow clouds at every step and hangs in the air behind you. High above, slender towers lean together against the dim sky. The street runs east deeper into the city and west back toward the great wall.
rooms.8894: A dry fountain stands in the middle of this street, its basin cracked and its centrepiece a statue of a woman whose face has been chiselled away. Rags of banners that were once yellow hang from poles on the housefronts, faded almost to grey and stirring though there is no wind. Ahead to the east the street opens before a building of utter black. The way back runs west between the silent houses.
rooms.8895: The street opens here into a silent square before the Black Building, a windowless mass of stone so dark that it seems less a building than a hole cut in the dim air. Its only door, a slab of black metal without handle or hinge, stands in the east face. Streets lead north and south from the square, and the way back runs west. Underfoot the paving is laid in a spiral that winds toward the door.
rooms.8897: The street ends at the edge of the city, where a broken balustrade looks out over a vast, still lake. Mist lies on the water in long banks that roll slowly like waves of cloud, and on the far shore the towers of another city, or of this one, rise into the gloom. The black stars hang low over the lake. The only way back is south to the square.
rooms.8898: Within its black walls the building has no roof, and the dim sky with its black stars looks down into a vast empty court floored with glassy black stone. There is no furniture, no carving, no sign of what this place was for, only an enormous silence. In the centre of the floor a broad stair goes down into the earth, each step wide enough for a wagon. The door in the west wall leads back to the square.
rooms.8899: The stair ends in a vault so huge that its far walls are lost in darkness, and the air is warm and smells faintly of brimstone and old ash. In the centre lies a sarcophagus of black stone the length of a ship, its lid carved with a coiled dragon whose wings fold over the whole of it. Scales as wide as shields are set into the walls like tiles, each one of dull bronze. The only way out is the stair up to the Black Building.
rooms.8896: This street ends in a half-ruined theatre, its curved tiers of seats crumbling toward a stage where tatters of yellow cloth still hang from a fallen frame. The tiers are empty, yet the silence here has the held-breath feeling of an audience waiting. Masks of stone are carved along the rim of the stage, all of them pale and all of them smiling. The only way out is north, back to the square.
rooms.12055: The mayor's office is a comfortable, cluttered room panelled in honey-coloured wood, with a broad desk heaped with petitions, a pair of leather armchairs and a cabinet of rolled maps. A tall window of thick green glass lets in a watery light and the distant sounds of the harbour. Portraits of former mayors line the walls, each in a gilded frame and each looking more pleased with himself than the last. A door to the west leads back into the court clerk's office.
rooms.12060: Shelves of dark wood rise from floor to ceiling in this long room, crammed with bound ledgers whose spines are lettered by year: harbour dues, court judgements, deeds of sale and the manifests of every ship that has unloaded at Port Halyon. A long table runs down the middle, with high stools and lamps set inside glass chimneys to guard the paper. The air is dry and smells of dust and old ink. The court clerk's office lies north, and a second records room opens east.
rooms.212061: This inner records room holds the oldest papers in the port, and it shows: the shelves sag under scrolls in cracked leather cases and bundles of brittle parchment tied with faded ribbon. A great iron chest stands against the end wall, triple-locked, and above it hangs a framed chart of the coast as it was drawn long ago, with sea monsters coiled in its margins. Dust lies thick, broken only by a narrow trail of footprints. The only way out is west.
rooms.12037: The council of Port Halyon meets in this tall room around a great horseshoe table of polished oak, with a carved chair at its head for the Dock Master and lesser chairs along its arms. On the wall hangs a vast painted map of the harbour and the coast, its shipping lanes picked out in gold leaf. A wooden door to the north leads to the Dock Master's private office, a bronze door opens east into the entrance foyer, and tall double doors lead south.
rooms.12038: This smaller chamber is where the real business of the council gets done, around a round table scarred with the rings of countless wine cups. A slate board on one wall still bears the ghosts of chalked figures, half wiped away: tonnages, tariffs, the names of ships. The chairs are mismatched and comfortable, and a sideboard holds a row of empty decanters. The tall double doors to the north lead back into the Council Room.
rooms.12002: The guild that runs the games in the warehouse keeps its office in this narrow room above the benches, behind a screen of carved lattice through which the crowd can be watched unseen. A sloping desk holds the guild's great ledger, and the walls are hung with painted bills announcing bouts and races. A ladder climbs up to a trapdoor in the ceiling, and a steep stair leads down to the seating below. The muffled roar of the crowd rises through the floor.
rooms.12001: The guild chief's office is a cramped loft under the warehouse roof, reached only by the trapdoor in its floor. Its walls are covered with slates on which the results of every bout and race are chalked in columns, alongside odds, wagers and debts owed. A small round window looks out over the fighting ground far below. A strongbox is bolted to the floor beside a battered desk, and the trapdoor leads down to the guild office.
rooms.12009: The basement of the main warehouse is no cellar but a vast sunken yard, open to the sky, with the warehouse's galleries rising in tiers of timber and stone on every side. This corner of the yard is given over to practice: wooden posts hacked to splinters, straw dummies on poles and a rack of blunted spears chained to the wall. The ground is a mix of trampled grass and sand. The yard stretches east along the track and south toward the far corner.
rooms.12016: A tall turning post of painted stone marks this corner of the sunken yard, and around it the chariot track swings in a tight curve, rutted deep by wheels and churned by hooves. The outer wall here is scarred and splintered where chariots have taken the bend too fast. High above, the galleries lean over the yard, and the sky shows grey between their eaves. The track runs south toward the stables and west along the yard.
rooms.212017: Here the warehouse's upper floor juts out over the corner of the yard, roofing it with heavy beams, and beneath them the chariot teams are stabled. Stalls of rough planking line the walls, and harness hangs from pegs in tangles of leather and brass. The air is warm and thick with the smells of horse, straw and liniment. The yard opens north along the track and west toward the practice ground.
rooms.12008: The supervisor of the warehouse keeps his office here in the open air, on a platform built out from the roof above the galleries and shaded by a canvas awning that snaps in the sea wind. A heavy table is bolted to the planks, and a speaking trumpet of brass hangs on a hook beside it. From the rail you can see the whole sunken yard spread below, and beyond the roofs the masts of the harbour. A stair leads down into the galleries.
rooms.12034: South Main Street runs broad and busy here between tall houses of whitewashed stone, their shutters painted the blue of the harbour. A narrow shopfront to the east is hung with bunches of dried herbs and a sign of a silver crescent moon, where the Mage's Shop does its trade. West, a gravelled lane turns off into the Wealthy Neighborhood. The street runs north to the intersection with River Avenue and south to the South Gate.
rooms.12027: A gravelled lane winds between clipped hedges and iron railings here, past lawns so green they seem to have been painted. Through gates of wrought iron you glimpse gardens of roses, fountains and fig trees. To the south rises the great house of the Dock Master, its marble face blazing white, and to the west the mayor's house stands behind a row of cypresses. The lane leads north to River Avenue and east to South Main Street.
rooms.12021: The mayor's house is grand in a slightly anxious way, as if straining to keep up with the Dock Master's mansion across the lane. Its hall is floored in chequered marble and hung with tapestries of ships and sea battles, and a long table gleams with silver beneath a chandelier of coloured glass. The air smells of beeswax and lavender. The front door leads east, back out into the Wealthy Neighborhood.
rooms.212006: Blades of every kind cover the walls of this shop, hung on pegs in fans and rows: cutlasses, boarding axes, long knives and heavy sabres, all oiled and gleaming. A long counter of scarred oak stands before a grindstone, and the smell of oil and hot steel hangs in the air. A door in the west wall leads into the back room, where the stock is kept. The street door opens north onto River Avenue.
rooms.205071: A spine of red rock breaks out of the sand here, a ridge of weathered stone that the wind has carved into fins and hollows. The trail scrambles over it on ledges worn smooth by the feet of camels. From the crest the dunes roll away under a white, blazing sky, broken far off by the point of a pyramid. Heat beats up from the rock as from a forge, and the trail drops north and south onto the sand.

12122.description: The letters read: HERE YOU WILL BE ASKED ONCE. Beneath them, in a smaller and shakier hand, someone has scratched: AND THEN AGAIN, AND AGAIN.

12190.description: The lantern is fitted with a hinged iron hood worked by a chain, so that whoever holds the chain can show a light to the sea and hide it from the land in the same moment. The glass is clean and the wick freshly trimmed.

12128.description: The eye is carved deep and painted white, with a black pupil that seems to follow you whichever way you turn. Scraps of parchment are nailed beneath it, bearing prayers, curses and the names of the missing.

12134.description: The list runs on and on: TOLAN, DROWNING. MERREN, THE DARK. ASCH, HER FATHER. Some of the newest names have nothing carved after them yet.

12199.description: The idol's six hands hold a wine cup, a pair of dice, a fat purse, a sweetmeat, a key and a mask. Its gilt has been rubbed from its belly by the palms of those who touch it for luck, leaving the bare wood dark and greasy.

12204.description: The mask is taller than three men, hammered from sheets of silver riveted together. Its hollow eyes are set with black glass, and when the braziers flare a low moan seems to sound from somewhere within its open mouth.

12191.description: Each plinth bears a small brass plate engraved with a name and a date. The faces are made with horrible care, down to the pores of the skin and the tears on the cheeks, and some of the hair looks very much like real hair.

12143.description: The cairn is built from the stones of the fallen road. A line has been scratched into the topmost stone: THE ROAD GOES ON, BUT NOT FOR YOU.

15101.description: The fish-eyed faces wear crowns of shells and coral, and between them runs a line of writing in no script you know. The bronze is pitted by salt, but the carving is still sharp, as if its makers meant it to outlast them.

8861.description: A man's height above the water, the tallest pillar is ringed by a band of carving: a crowned figure standing with arms outstretched while storms rage on every side. Sailors say Stethelos was a sea-king who bound the winds here, and that the pillars are the posts of his drowned hall.

8834.description: The head wears a tall crown of tapering points, and its features are not quite those of any people you know: the brow too high, the eyes set too far apart. Its lips are parted as if it died in the middle of a word.

8803.description: The tower's stones are blackened by smoke and salt. Above its door a weathered plaque reads: KEEP THE LIGHT AND THE LIGHT KEEPS YOU.

8886.description: The figures climb the pillars in a spiral toward the keystone: crowned men and women first, then robed ones, then shapes that are less and less like people. On the keystone itself is carved a single tower beneath a crescent of black stars.

8888.description: Where the words can still be made out, each step bears a single one, and read in order they make a kind of prayer: DO NOT LOOK DOWN, DO NOT LOOK BACK, THE STAIR IS THERE IF YOU BELIEVE IT.

8895.description: The door is cold enough to sting the fingers. When you lay your palm against it, you hear, very faintly, the sound of something enormous breathing far below.

8899.description: The carved dragon's eyes are closed, but the lid has been shifted a hand's breadth from its place, and the stone at the gap is scored with deep, parallel grooves like the marks of claws.

212061.description: The old chart shows Port Halyon as a cluster of huts beside a river mouth. Far out to sea, among the drawn monsters, a ring of black pillars is labelled in faded red ink: HERE THE SEA GOES DOWN.

creatures.long_desc: A weather-beaten smuggler watches the path, one hand resting on the knife at his belt.
creatures.description: A lean, sun-blackened man in a tarred coat and grey sharkskin boots, his hair tied back with a strip of sailcloth. A coil of rope hangs over one shoulder and a shuttered lantern swings at his hip, and his eyes keep straying toward the sea. He has the look of someone who would much rather you had not seen him at all.

creatures.long_desc: A hammerhead shark cruises just beneath the surface, its tall fin slicing through the swell.
creatures.description: A long, grey-backed shark with a pale belly and a head flattened into a broad blade, an unblinking eye set at each end of it. Old scars criss-cross its hide, and when it turns you glimpse rows of small, serrated teeth in its crescent of a mouth. It swings its strange head from side to side as it swims, as if tasting the water for blood.

creatures.long_desc: A great sea serpent rears out of the water, its coils looping through the waves like the keels of overturned boats.
creatures.description: The serpent is longer than any ship in Port Halyon, its body as thick as a barrel and armoured in overlapping scales of green-black that shimmer with oily rainbows. Its head is long and narrow like a pike's, crowned with a frill of spines, and its eyes glow the same cold, pale green as the stones of the drowned gate. Barnacles crust the oldest of its scales.

creatures.long_desc: A cultist of terror stands here in black robes, a screaming mask hiding its face.
creatures.description: A figure in heavy robes of black wool, belted with a cord of knotted red silk, its face hidden behind a mask of white lacquer carved into an endless scream. Through the eyeholes you glimpse eyes that are perfectly calm. Its pale hands are flecked with candle wax, and a curved knife hangs from the cord at its waist.
rooms: Entrance To The Temple Of Terror
Entrance To The Office Of The High Priest Of Terror

creatures.long_desc: A wax effigy of a screaming man lurches stiffly forward, its glass eyes rolling.
creatures.description: From a distance it might be one of the figures from the Hall of Wax, and up close it is: a life-size man moulded in yellowish wax, every pore and eyelash in place, its mouth stretched in a silent scream. Something has woken it. It moves in jerky, uncertain steps, leaving soft smears of wax on whatever it touches, and its glass eyes roll to follow you.
rooms: Office Of The High Priest Of Terror

creatures.long_desc: A shade of Carcosa drifts silently through the dim air, trailing tatters of darkness.
creatures.description: It has the shape of a tall figure robed in grey, but the shape is thin and wavering, like a reflection in dark water, and you can see the stones of the city through it. Where its face should be there is only a smooth pale oval, like a mask without features. It makes no sound at all, and the air around it is cold enough to numb your fingers.
rooms: In The Streets Of Dim Carcosa
The Tomb Of The Father Of All Dragons

items.room_desc: A sailor's knife with a tarred grip lies here.
items.description: A straight, broad-backed knife with a keen point and a grip bound in tarred cord, made for cutting rope and gutting fish. A hole bored through the pommel holds a lanyard, so that it cannot be lost overboard.

items.room_desc: A pair of grey sharkskin boots lies here.
items.description: Knee-high boots of grey sharkskin, rough as a file against the grain and smooth as silk with it, stitched with waxed gut. The rough soles grip a wet deck or a slick rock as surely as bare feet.

items.room_desc: A white lacquered mask, carved into a scream, stares up from the ground.
items.description: A mask of white-lacquered wood carved into a face of utter terror, its mouth wide and its brows drawn up in anguish. The inside is lined with black felt and smells of incense and sweat. Behind it your own face feels very far away.

items.room_desc: A great green-black scale, curved like a shield, lies here.
items.description: A single scale from a sea serpent's flank, as broad as a man's chest and curved like a buckler. Its thick, horny root makes a natural grip, and its surface shimmers green and black with oily rainbows that blades skid across as off wet stone.

items.room_desc: A heavy coin of greenish gold lies here, catching no light.
items.description: A thick coin of dull, greenish gold, heavier than it ought to be, stamped on one face with a tall tower beneath a sky of black stars. The other face, where a king's head would be, is blank and smooth. It is cold to the touch and stays cold however long you hold it.
